name: matmul

verdict.line: latency-bound (neither roof): 38% of the matrix peak, 33% of the cache-resident rate (past the L2); matrix core 43% busy; issue-bound at 1 wave(s) a SIMD (lds): the matrix core idles 34% while its waves issue the loop's 2.4 other instructions per matrix one; matrix core idle before the main loop 7% (one workgroup a CU: not hidden); matrix core idle after the main loop 4% (one workgroup a CU: not hidden); L2 re-fetch: 4.0x the call's bytes cross it

findings.text: latency-bound (neither roof): 38% of the matrix peak, 33% of the cache-resident rate (past the L2)

issue-bound: 1 wave(s) a SIMD (bound by lds), and the main loop issues 2.4 other instructions per matrix one (32 vmem_lds, 64 ds_read, 76 valu, 116 salu against 128); the matrix core idles 34% of the kernel with its waves issuing them
the matrix core idles 20% of the kernel with its waves at vmem_issue (at buffer/global loads and stores: the address/data path is busy)
the matrix core idles 8% of the kernel with its waves at valu (at vector ALU instructions (their dependencies, or the VALU busy))

prologue: the matrix core idles 7% of the kernel while the waves are before the main loop (515 instructions: 193 VALU, 32 loads); at one workgroup a slot no other workgroup's main loop overlaps it, so it adds to the kernel's time
the matrix core idles 7% of the kernel with its waves at scalar (at scalar ALU and scalar-memory instructions)
the matrix core idles 6% of the kernel with its waves at lds_issue (at ds_read/ds_write: the LDS queue or bandwidth (or bank conflicts))

epilogue: the matrix core idles 4% of the kernel while the waves are after the main loop (drain + epilogue) (849 instructions: 283 VALU, 64 stores); at one workgroup a slot no other workgroup's main loop overlaps it, so it adds to the kernel's time

findings.short: L2 re-fetch: 4.0x the call's bytes cross it
findings.text: the L2 re-fetches: 873 MB cross it, 4.0x the call's inputs and outputs (33% of the cache-resident rate): tiles shared by workgroups on different XCDs/L2s, or evicted before their reuse

verdict.line: latency-bound (neither roof): 38% of the matrix peak, 33% of the cache-resident rate (past the L2); matrix core 43% busy; issue-bound at 1 wave(s) a SIMD (lds): the matrix core idles 34% while its waves issue the loop's 2.4 other instructions per matrix one; matrix core idle before the main loop 7% (one workgroup a CU: not hidden); matrix core idle after the main loop 4% (one workgroup a CU: not hidden); L2 re-fetch: 4.0x the call's bytes cross it

cannot: MALL (Infinity Cache) hits: the L2's misses all count as requests to the fabric (TCC_EA0_RDREQ_DRAM = TCC_EA0_RDREQ); a MALL hit and an HBM read look alike, so `dram_bytes` is bytes past the L2

stall reasons by instruction: the counters give the share of wave time waiting for a dependency (s_waitcnt, barrier) or to issue, not which; the thread trace (att) attributes them per instruction on one CU

ceilings.source: MI355X measured (hk.integration.headroom.PEAKS: a register-only v_mfma bf16 loop on every CU, 2.47-2.48 PFLOP/s; a 1 GiB read past the 256 MB Infinity Cache, 6.54-6.60 TB/s); cache-resident 9.1 TB/s (hk.check.CARDS). fp8 is 2x bf16 (datasheet ratio, not measured)

compare.line: hipblaslt takes 0.576x the time of matmul (interleaved in one process: 176.7 vs 304.7 us, band 6%); profiled calls: hipblaslt 181.9 us vs matmul 294.7 us (0.617x the time); matrix core idle after the main loop (drain + epilogue) 3.6% -> 7.3% of the kernel; matrix core busy 43% -> 78%; matrix idle at VALU 8% -> 4%; VALU instructions 3.002e+07 -> 1.936e+07; workgroups 2,048 -> 256; loop instructions per matrix one 2.43 -> 0.777; CUs busy 94% -> 89%
